subject: Clarify: routing/multipool routing & SOC 2 scope - hosted vs dedicated
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmebank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmebank.com
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 applicability question for multipool routing

Hi Olga,

Quick question from our security review: we see Redwood offers Hosted endpoints and Dedicated GPU pools. Our integration would use a dedicated pool but we understand some traffic routing may pass through a multipool fronting layer for failover and cost routing.

For SOC 2 Type II applicability, will Acme Bank be considered "in-scope" only for the Dedicated pool, or does any shared/multipool routing tier that sees request metadata make the Hosted environment in-scope as well?

If Hosted components are considered in-scope because of ephemeral routing, can you provide (a) the most recent Type II report, (b) a bridge letter for any Hosted-to-Dedicated split during the audit period, and (c) a simple diagram showing which components would need evidence?

We are trying to finalize our purchase approval this week, so a short answer + attachments would be hugely helpful.

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Acme Bank

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmebank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 applicability question for multipool routing

Tom — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: scope depends on whether any Hosted-tier component has access to request payloads or user-identifying metadata during the audit period. In our common setup, routing decisions are made by a lightweight fronting layer that only passes anonymized routing headers and does not persist request payloads; in that configuration we can support a bridge letter and keep Hosted runtime controls scoped out of your Dedicated-environment Type II evidence.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Neha to confirm controls/evidence and to attach the latest Type II and a draft bridge letter. Ben — FYI, procurement timeline comment from Acme.

Next steps:
- Kimberly/Neha: confirm routing telemetry retained during 2025 audit window and whether any metadata copies land in Hosted logs.
- I will attach the 2025 Type II and a topology diagram plus a bridge-letter draft.
- Tom: can you confirm the approximate cutover date for your Dedicated pool (est. start of production)? We may need alignment for the audit period mapping.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmebank.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC2 applicability question for multipool routing

Forwarding our quick findings. Key points for the thread:

- Logging: the fronting/routing tier records a routing decision id and short-lived route tag. It does NOT persist full request bodies or customer PII in Hosted logs.
- KV cache: Hosted runtime may keep encrypted KV for global models; however, Dedicated pool KV is segregated when the customer uses Dedicated. No cross-tenant KV access.
- Evidence we can provide: 2025 Type II report (full report redacted per standard), architecture diagram (routing/topology), log retention and redaction policy excerpt, and a one-page bridge letter that states Hosted routing layer did not hold customer payloads during the 2025 window.

Attachments I'm pushing to the thread: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2025.pdf, redwood-routing-topology-2026.png, bridge-letter-template.docx.

Recommended language for Acme's auditor: we can sign a bridge letter certifying no persistent customer payloads were handled by Hosted runtime for traffic routed to Dedicated pools during the stated audit period; we will also supply redaction policy and sampling evidence.

If Acme needs Hosted-run evidence regardless (auditor asks for it), we can scope those Hosted controls into the engagement — there is a lead time for evidence pulls (~7 business days).

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmebank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmebank.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 applicability question for multipool routing

Thanks — that is exactly the clarity we needed.

Acme's timeline: planned Dedicated pool onboarding 2026-06-15 (prod cutover). Our auditor has asked us to provide evidence for the period Jan 1 2025 — Dec 31 2025. Per Kimberly's note, if your bridge letter states Hosted layer did not store customer payloads during that 2025 window that should be sufficient for us to treat only the Dedicated pool as in-scope.

Please send the Type II PDF and the bridge-letter draft as soon as you can. Procurement will look for a DocuSign-ready bridge letter; procurement contact is procurement@acmebank.com.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Tom
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Acme Bank
